title: Positive-rank top cohomology of a normalized conormal comparison
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $r\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ with $(f)=I$. Suppose a basis $b$ of $I/I^2$ over $B=A/I$ is indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ and satisfies $b_i=f_i\bmod I^2$ [def-sc-koszul-conormal-comparison]. Let $\varphi$ be an $A$-linear cochain map from the signed dual Koszul complex [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex] to $\bigwedge_B^r\operatorname{Hom}_B(I/I^2,B)$ concentrated in degree $r$, satisfying the determinant normalization [def-sc-koszul-conormal-comparison]. The induced map $H^r(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism. No Koszul-regularity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, local signed dual Koszul computation; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQZ

proof.text: Evaluation on the standard top wedge is injective by applying Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det directly to the two alternating maps and using equality of their values on the standard basis, and surjective by the top exterior basis coordinate. Expand d_r of that wedge using koszul_differential. Its complementary ordered wedges have coefficients (-1)^(i.val+2) f_i. The corresponding determinant pairing functionals take value 1 on their own complementary wedge and 0 on all the others. After the dual sign (-1)^r, multiplication by the inverse unit sign gives each f_i in the image of evaluation of the incoming differential. Every incoming value belongs to (f), and the image is a submodule; hence it equals I. Injectivity of top evaluation and Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem identify incoming boundaries with the kernel of reduced top evaluation.

The top exterior basis of the dual conormal module has a single vector: powersetCard (Fin r) r is a singleton. Pairing this vector with the ordered conormal basis wedge is 1. Basis.sum_repr therefore makes evaluation at that wedge bijective. Apply the determinant normalization to the standard free basis vectors; hb identifies their conormal classes with b. The component has paired value epsilon times the reduced top evaluation, with epsilon^2=1. Surjectivity of A to A/I and of top evaluation proves that the component is surjective, and injectivity of determinant evaluation identifies its kernel with the reduced top-evaluation kernel. This proof also works when I=A or A is the zero ring.

The next exterior power vanishes because powersetCard (Fin r) (r+1) is empty. Its dual term is also zero, so the outgoing differential in degree r is zero. The target single complex has both differentials zero.

Pass to the short complexes in degree r. Mathlib ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_isIso_descOpcycles reduces the homology map to the map out of the incoming cokernel. Its surjectivity follows from the component surjectivity. For injectivity, lift the difference of two cokernel classes along pOpcycles; if its image is zero, steps 1 and 2 place this lift in the incoming range, so moduleCat_pOpcycles_eq_zero_iff kills its class. ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective gives the isomorphism, and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff gives the desired homology isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem koszul_conormal_comparison_isIso_top_homology_pos
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hr : 0 < r) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (A ⧸ I) I.Cotangent)
    (hb : ∀ i, b i = koszulConormalVector A I r f hf (Finsupp.single i 1))
    (φ : koszulDualComplex A r f ⟶
      (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat A) (ComplexShape.up ℕ) r).obj
        (koszulNormalDeterminant A I r))
    (hφ : IsKoszulConormalComparison A I r f hf φ) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap φ r)
